extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark of 3,002 high-school geometry problems with dense formal language annotations for problem text and diagrams.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Problems were manually collected from two online digital libraries containing popular high-school textbooks, and each problem was annotated with problem text, diagram, answer choices, correct answer, problem goal, geometry shapes, and dense formal language descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems collected from two popular high-school textbooks accessed via the online digital libraries McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into train, validation, and test sets with a 0.7:0.1:0.2 ratio.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2. For human performance evaluation on the test split, annotators who did not satisfy the time requirements were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem’s text, diagram, four answer choices, and correct answer, labeled each problem with problem goal and geometry shapes, and annotated dense formal language descriptions for text and diagrams.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human performance evaluation, annotators were filtered based on degree and time requirements to ensure effort and eligibility.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees collected and labeled the dataset; human evaluation annotators on Amazon Mechanical Turk were required to have a high school or higher degree; additional human experts were graduates majoring in science or engineering.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project with code and data is available at https://lupantech.github.io/inter-gps . The paper states, "In order to promote follow-up work in the geometry domain, we release the dataset and evaluation baselines."
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is drawn from high-school textbooks for grades 6–12, which may bias it toward SAT-style school geometry problems and textbook distributions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations in parser and solver performance, including failures on ambiguous diagram annotations, multiple primitives, nested expressions, uncertain references, and complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, training, validation, and testing geometry problem solvers, including parsers and symbolic reasoning systems.

name.evidence: Thus, we construct a new large-scale benchmark, Geometry3K, consisting of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language.

description.evidence: To overcome these challenges, we first construct a new large-scale benchmark, called Geometry3K, to assess algorithms’ performance of geometry problem solving. The Geometry3K dataset consists of 3,002 multi-choice problems as well as covers diverse geometric shapes and problem goals. In contrast with existing work, we also annotate each problem text and diagram with unified structural descriptions in formal language.

We filter out annotators who do not satisfy the requirement.
